what_happened: S009's counterexample search produced a genuine, minimal counterexample showing that the S008 reduction rule R1 ('a legal setFact/relocate keeps the LAST write per (subject, predicate) cell') is not semantics-preserving. On a valid canon whose cell holds two simultaneously-effective facts (overlapping validity windows), the 3-intervention history [setFact(W1), retractFact(f2), setFact(W2)] derives differently after reduction: legacy yields derived:["char/x","at"]=W2 (hash 2eaa050a) while the reduced chain yields fact/x-at-loc1=W2 (hash f41330b7). semanticEqual=false, hashEqual=false, diffEmpty=false.
root_cause: R1 assumes a write's effect is fully determined by the last write to its cell. That holds only when a cell holds at most one effective fact (a write leaves one derived fact whose id the next write reuses). When a cell holds multiple simultaneously-effective facts, overrideFact (world-state.ts:190) selects the LAST matching fact by validFrom and reuses its id. A retractFact of that fact between two writes changes which id the later write reuses, so dropping the earlier write changes the surviving fact's IDENTITY. The facts dimension of the effective semantic representation is keyed by fact id, so this is a semantic difference, not a lineage one.
what_i_did_wrong: In S008 I wrote R1 from the effective-fact cell semantics alone ('last write wins') and validated it on the seed canons, whose multi-fact cells have disjoint windows. I treated 'multi-fact cell' as the attack surface but concluded it was safe because the seed canons never have two facts effective at once — instead of asking whether the ENGINE permits two facts effective at once. It does (overrideFact explicitly handles multiple matching facts). S008's 1632/1632 pass rate was real but did not cover this configuration, and I over-read it as general soundness.
detection: S009 formalized R1 with its assumptions and built a synthetic canon with overlapping windows (ev/a root occurs; ev/b in a REQUIRES cycle is unfounded so does not occur). experiments/s009/probe-overlap.ts then showed the divergence; experiments/s009/probe-minimize.ts baked the overlap into the canon to reduce the history to 3 interventions and confirmed the canon passes inspectCanon with zero errors.
impact: The reduction is NOT a universally legitimate semantic abstraction. It is sound for canons with at most one effective fact per cell (the seed canons), which is not an enforced precondition. S008's productionization recommendation must be qualified accordingly.
fix_status: Not applied by design. S009's specification requires reporting BLOCKED rather than patching around a counterexample. A candidate correction (the 'multi-fact guard': refuse to subsume an earlier legal write to a cell if a retractFact of one of that cell's canon facts occurred between them) is documented in qms/records/nonconformities/ncr-006 and verified to repair the counterexample, but is left for a separate productionization task.
lesson: When formalizing a reduction rule, state the assumption it rests on and then ask whether the ENGINE guarantees that assumption — not merely whether the current fixtures satisfy it. A high pass rate on fixtures is evidence of coverage, not of soundness. The seed canons' disjoint windows hid an engine-supported configuration the rule cannot handle.
